events.source_name: Museum of Art and Digital Entertainment (MADE)
events.title: Open Projector Nights
events.why: A no-polish-required public slot for unfinished games, code, poems, doodles, and other strange prototypes—an especially useful low-stakes entry point into Oakland's game-art scene.

events.title: Leonardo Art/Science Evening Rendezvous
events.why: Three free talks turn real and artificial minds, AI and artists, and satirical art into a good excuse for an actual mixed-discipline room.

events.source_name: Museum of Art and Digital Entertainment (MADE)
events.title: Experimental Play Nights
events.why: The MADE's monthly invitation to play elaborate, strange games is a compact antidote to showroom-demo creative culture.

events.title: Tank Houses in Northwest Berkeley
events.why: An architect-led three-mile hunt for six surviving windmill-topped water tanks—an overlooked East Bay infrastructure ghost story.

events.price_note: $23 single night; $60 festival pass; free or discounted for members
events.title: San Francisco Electronic Music Festival Night 3: Moor Mother, Seth Cluett, Thomas Carnacki
events.why: Moor Mother's Afrofuturist fusion of noise, rap, and free jazz anchors an experimental-music night that also moves through immersive found-sound and unconventional-object work.

events.title: Algorithmic Art Assembly presents: Kit Clayton
events.why: A key Bay Area Max/MSP and Jitter developer joins an out-there computer-music lineup with experimental electronics and a SuperCollider talk-performance.

events.title: Gray Area x TIAT: Processing Community Day: San Francisco
events.why: A genuinely communal creative-code afternoon: 25 years of Processing, p5.js typography, an experimental WebGPU renderer, talks, and participation rather than a platform-sales pitch.

events.title: Unseen Visions: A New Age Music and Culture Symposium
events.why: New Age media archaeology becomes something richer here: Robert Rich, Belson and Fadiman films, an SF radio history, and Erik Davis in a two-day performance-and-ideas program.

events.title: Micro To Macro: Microorganisms, Sound and Robots
events.why: The clearest machine-art bullseye: living bacteria, plants, and tiny crustaceans drive custom electronics, robots, sound, and a participatory plant orchestra.
